title: Are millionaires really leaving Massachusetts? We don’t know yet.
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: IRS data needed to track millionaire migration after the 2023 surtax isn't available yet, fueling ongoing debate.
Massachusetts saw a net outflow of 30,000 people by mid-2025, but it's unclear if high earners are leaving.
The 4% surtax generated $3.4 billion in fiscal 2025, funding education and transportation, but migration impacts remain uncertain.

title: 7 things to do during a rainy day on the Cape
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: The Chatham Shark Center offers interactive exhibits and activities for families interested in learning about sharks in Cape Cod waters.
Visitors to Cape Cod can explore museums like the John F. Kennedy Hyannis Museum and historic homes such as the Hoxie House.
Cape Playhouse in Dennis hosts performances, while the Chatham Orpheum Theater offers daily free kids matinees during inclement weather.

title: Visit to Boston made Boca Raton resident feel miserable about living in Boca Raton
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Ian Pinto felt miserable about Boca Raton after visiting Boston from July 31 to August 3.
Pinto praised Boston's walkability, public transport, and affordability compared to Boca Raton.
Pinto appreciated Boston's welcoming community and hopes to move there with his girlfriend.

title: Motorcyclist killed in crash with pickup truck in Raynham
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Jason Marshall, 31, from Taunton died in a motorcycle collision with a pickup on Route 138, Raynham.
The accident involved a 1999 Suzuki TL 1000 motorcycle and a 2015 Chevy Silverado pickup truck.
The pickup driver, 57, stayed at the scene; police and State Police Detectives are investigating.

title: N.H. police seek to identify suspects who fatally shot dog in attempted armed robbery
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A dog was fatally shot during an attempted armed robbery in Hollis, New Hampshire early Tuesday morning.
The victim had arranged to meet a supposed female online, but was confronted by a man and woman with a gun.
Hollis police seek public help in identifying the suspects, asking for security footage from nearby residents.

title: Former Red Sox infielder criticized front office: ‘Some people watch the game, some people go on the computer’
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Vaughn Grissom criticized Red Sox for relying too much on analytics over player observation.
Traded by Red Sox, Grissom is now a regular starter with the Angels, batting .254 in 2026.
Despite criticisms, Grissom expressed no hard feelings towards his former Boston teammates.

title: Authorities investigating 4 family members shot in N.H. as potential attempted murders and suicide
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Four family members were shot in a New Hampshire home early Tuesday morning, officials are investigating it as attempted murder-suicide.
Eric Blake Jr., 29, died from a gunshot wound to the head, ruled a suicide by the Medical Examiner's office.
Amy Blake, 59, and Michael Marro, 41, remain in critical condition; Eric Blake Sr., 53, is stable after self-reporting to a hospital.

title: Livestream: Lindsay Clancy murder trial continues with her psychiatric treatment in the spotlight
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Duxbury Police Officer Cameron Daley testified about guarding Lindsay Clancy in the hospital following her suicide attempt.
Licensed mental health counselor Latiesha Dukes testified about Clancy's postpartum anxiety and lack of a suicide plan.
Massachusetts State Police Sgt. Daniel Lawlor confirmed a court order was needed for a psychologist to visit Clancy in hospital.

title: Acton teen charged with murder used ChatGPT for ‘fantasies’ about killing family, DA says
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Arjun Aravind, 17, was arrested and charged with the murder of his mother Sudha Venkatesan and brother Siddarth in Acton.
Authorities reported that Aravind used ChatGPT to create stories and ideas about killing his family before the alleged murders.
Aravind was found in Wayland in a stolen vehicle and arrested without incident; he awaits arraignment on murder charges.

title: Q&A: Boston’s nightlife czar says the city is just getting started
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Boston's nightlife is expanding with initiatives like social districts and extended operating hours, aiming to boost the city's 24-hour economy.
Director of Nightlife Economy Corean Reynolds reports positive feedback from businesses and visitors following summer pilots and extended alcohol service.
Challenges include securing permanent legislation for relaxed alcohol laws and enhancing late-night transportation options for workers.
